title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 5
statement: Elmer the emu takes \(44\) equal strides to walk between consecutive telephone poles on a rural road. Oscar the ostrich can cover the same distance in \(12\) equal leaps. The telephone poles are evenly spaced, and the \(41\)st pole along this road is exactly one mile (\(5280\) feet) from the first pole. How much longer, in feet, is Oscar’s leap than Elmer’s stride?

solutions.text:
There are \(40\) gaps between the first and \(41\)st poles, so each gap is \(\dfrac{5280}{40} = 132\) feet.

Elmer’s stride is \(\dfrac{132}{44} = 3\) feet and Oscar’s leap is \(\dfrac{132}{12} = 11\) feet, a difference of \(11 - 3 = 8\) feet.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: From the first pole to the \(41\)st pole there are \(40\) gaps, so each gap is \(\dfrac{5280}{40}\) feet
Elmer’s stride is one gap divided by \(44;\) Oscar’s leap is one gap divided by \(12\)
